title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-27-jordan-patel
content:
Daily scratchpad - applied ML experiments (quant + eval)
Date: 2026-03-27
Owner: Jordan Patel
Quick context:
- Trying to get 4-bit GPTQ quantization stable on the rlhf-finetuned family (llama2-style checkpoints we onboarded). Goal: <5% delta on helpfulness eval (MRR/accuracy) while reducing VRAM by ~2x.
- Current best baseline: full-fp16 LlamaX-13B (finetuned) on eval set: MRR=0.642, EM=0.49, avg latency=210ms (p2.xlarge equiv).
Notes / open questions:
- bnb 4-bit (nf4) vs GPTQ 4-bit (per-channel) — stability tradeoffs. Users reported hallucination increase with aggressive group size. Need to test group_size=128, 256, 512.
- Do we keep float16 KV cache or quantize KV caches too? Prefer keeping KV cache fp16 for latency but still background test quantized KV.
- Prompt sensitivity: shorter prompts (<=512 tokens) maintain quality better on quantized models. Longer-context behavior degrades. Need systematic prompt set.
Experiment plan for today:
1) Re-run GPTQ (gptq-0.4) with group_size=256, per-channel, calibrated on 512-sample calibration set (from eval/promptset-v2).
   - checkpoint: models/llamaX-13B-rlhf-v3.ckpt
   - cmd: python tools/gptq.py --input models/llamaX-13B-rlhf-v3.ckpt --bits 4 --group-size 256 --calib calib/512_random.json --out models/llamaX-13B-rlhf-v3-gptq-g256-4bit.safetensors
2) Baseline eval: run eval harness on full-fp16 baseline to have fresh numbers (seeded). Save run id.
   - cmd: python eval/harness.py --model models/llamaX-13B-rlhf-v3.fp16 --prompts eval/promptset-v2.json --out results/baseline-2026-03-27.json --seed 42
3) Quantized eval: run batch scoring for gptq result and bnb-nf4 variant. Measure MRR, EM, avg latency, 95th p99 latency, and tok/s.
   - cmd: python eval/harness.py --model models/llamaX-13B-rlhf-v3-gptq-g256-4bit.safetensors --prompts eval/promptset-v2.json --out results/gptq-g256-4bit-2026-03-27.json --measure-latency
4) Quick manual checks: sample 20 prompts from promptset-v2 with both models, paste responses to scratch block below for eyeballing hallucination and verbosity differences.
Quick results (first-pass, rough):
- Baseline run (fresh): MRR=0.645, EM=0.488, avg latency=208ms
- GPTQ g=256 4-bit (local GPU): MRR=0.621 (-3.8%), EM=0.46 (-2.8%), avg latency=135ms (win)
- bnb-nf4 4-bit: MRR=0.627 (-2.8%), EM=0.47 (-3.6%), avg latency=128ms
Observations:
- Both quant methods give nice latency/VRAM wins; accuracy drop in 2.8-3.8% MRR range — within our soft target but need to check failure modes (certain prompt types fail more).
- Multi-turn/dialog prompts seem to lose coherence more often on GPTQ variant. Might be due to KV quantization inference path — verify KV kept fp16.
- Generated token distributions: quantized models favor shorter answers on some instruction prompts. Could be beam/search or temperature differences; check sampling RNG/params match baseline exactly.
Commands/ops notes:
- Ensure runtime uses --use-fp16-kv-cache for quant eval when possible. Our runtime flag: --kv-cache-fp16=true
- Profiling: run with --trace-kv-cache to verify cache loads are zero-copy vs memcpy (measured memcpy adds ~4ms per step).
- Memory: GPTQ file size reduced from 26GB -> 8.2GB on disk (safetensors). Good for Dedicated pool packing.
Manual sample checks (copy-paste outputs):
- Prompt #12 (faq-style): baseline answer concise and correct; gptq answered with correct facts but added an extra hallucinated step about auth tokens. bnb-nf4 matched baseline better.
- Prompt #5 (multi-turn): baseline preserved context across turns; gptq reset a piece of context after turn 3 (loses last user name). Suspect tokenization offset or KV eviction bug.
To-do (next 48h):
- [ ] Re-run GPTQ with group_size=128 and 512 to compare. Log differences and pick optimal group_size.
- [ ] Run targeted eval split by prompt type: faq, code, multi-turn, math. Create chart of delta vs baseline.
- [ ] Re-run eval with strict RNG/sampling parity check (same temp, top_p, seed) to rule out sampling variance.
- [ ] Investigate KV cache handling in our runtime: verify fp16 paths and ensure no accidental re-quantization. File bug if necessary (linked_artifacts JIRA-ML-893).
- [ ] Run a small red-team check for hallucination on top 50 user-facing prompts.
Notes-to-self (short):
- If group_size smaller -> expect slightly higher quality, larger size -> faster quantization speed but more error.
- Consider hybrid quant: first n layers in fp16, last layers quantized (common trick). Test n=6/8 cutoff.
- Keep a diff of token-level log probs to detect calibration drift.
Misc commands I ran today (history):
- git checkout quant-debug && git pull origin main
- CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python tools/gptq.py --input ... --bits 4 --group-size 256 
- python eval/harness.py --model ... --prompts eval/promptset-v2.json --out results/tmp.json --measure-latency
Linked refs:
- promptset-v2: eval/promptset-v2.json (mix of faq, multi-turn, code, math, 1500 prompts)
- calibration set: calib/512_random.json
Decisions / proposed:
- If gptq g=256 shows consistent ~<4% MRR drop and latency improvements, propose gating policy: route low-latency, non-critical routes to quantized model and keep critical routes on fp16. Add to routing policy doc (console-and-rollouts).
- For Dedicated customers wanting cost savings, offer quantized model pack option with clear performance delta in Console.
Last checkpoints / artifacts saved:
- results/baseline-2026-03-27.json
- results/gptq-g256-4bit-2026-03-27.json
- models/llamaX-13B-rlhf-v3-gptq-g256-4bit.safetensors

Notes to collaborators:

- Eli: can you check the runtime flags for kv-cache re-quantization? suspect codepath in runtime/kernel_dispatcher.cpp
-- Jordan
